Getting Started with huer

Source: vignettes/huer.Rmd
huer.Rmd

huer is an httr2-based R client for the Philips Hue CLIP API v2 and Hue Bridge Pro local HTTPS endpoints. It wraps all GET, POST, PUT, and DELETE resource operations across 41 CLIP v2 and Bridge Pro resource types, parses JSON envelopes into tidy tibble data frames via jsonlite, and provides clear diagnostics powered by cli.

Discovering and Authenticating with a Bridge

  1. Locate your bridge’s local IP address using hue_discover() (or check your router / Hue app).
  2. Press the physical round link button on top of the Hue Bridge.
  3. Generate an application key (hue-application-key) within 30 seconds:
library(huer)

bridges <- hue_discover()
ip <- bridges$internalipaddress[[1]]

# Press the physical link button on the Hue Bridge before running:
creds <- hue_create_app_key(ip, app_name = "huer")

# Store credentials for the current R session
hue_auth(ip = ip, app_key = creds$username[[1]], verify_ssl = FALSE)

For reproducible scripts, set HUE_BRIDGE_IP and HUE_APP_KEY in your environment, or create an explicit client object with hue_bridge():

library(huer)

bridge <- hue_bridge(
  ip = "192.168.1.50",
  app_key = "example-application-key",
  verify_ssl = FALSE
)
bridge
#> 
#> ── Philips Hue Bridge Client (CLIP API v2)
#> Bridge: https://192.168.1.50
#> App key: exam...-key
#> TLS: unverified (local)
#> Timeout: 10s

TLS Note: Local Philips Hue Bridges serve HTTPS using a certificate signed by the Signify Hue Bridge Root CA. For strict certificate validation, pass the path to the Signify Root CA PEM file via ca_cert with verify_ssl = TRUE; on trusted local LANs, verify_ssl = FALSE disables certificate verification.

Exploring All CLIP API v2 & Bridge Pro Endpoints

Use hue_endpoints() to inspect the complete matrix of supported resource types, REST paths, HTTP methods, and Bridge Pro / Hue Secure additions:

ep <- hue_endpoints()
nrow(ep)
#> [1] 41
head(ep, 10)
#> # A tibble: 10 × 8
#>    resource      category path               get   post  put   delete bridge_pro
#>    <chr>         <chr>    <chr>              <lgl> <lgl> <lgl> <lgl>  <lgl>     
#>  1 light         lighting /clip/v2/resource… TRUE  FALSE TRUE  FALSE  FALSE     
#>  2 grouped_light lighting /clip/v2/resource… TRUE  FALSE TRUE  FALSE  FALSE     
#>  3 room          groups   /clip/v2/resource… TRUE  TRUE  TRUE  TRUE   FALSE     
#>  4 zone          groups   /clip/v2/resource… TRUE  TRUE  TRUE  TRUE   FALSE     
#>  5 bridge_home   groups   /clip/v2/resource… TRUE  FALSE TRUE  FALSE  FALSE     
#>  6 service_group groups   /clip/v2/resource… TRUE  TRUE  TRUE  TRUE   TRUE      
#>  7 scene         scenes   /clip/v2/resource… TRUE  TRUE  TRUE  TRUE   FALSE     
#>  8 smart_scene   scenes   /clip/v2/resource… TRUE  TRUE  TRUE  TRUE   FALSE     
#>  9 device        devices  /clip/v2/resource… TRUE  FALSE TRUE  TRUE   FALSE     
#> 10 device_power  devices  /clip/v2/resource… TRUE  FALSE FALSE FALSE  FALSE

Filter for endpoints introduced for Hue Bridge Pro (such as MotionAware virtual motion areas, service_group, wifi_connectivity, speaker, and Hue Secure sensors):

ep[ep$bridge_pro, c("resource", "category", "get", "post", "put", "delete")]
#> # A tibble: 11 × 6
#>    resource                  category      get   post  put   delete
#>    <chr>                     <chr>         <lgl> <lgl> <lgl> <lgl> 
#>  1 service_group             groups        TRUE  TRUE  TRUE  TRUE  
#>  2 camera_motion             sensors       TRUE  FALSE TRUE  FALSE 
#>  3 bell_button               sensors       TRUE  FALSE FALSE FALSE 
#>  4 contact                   sensors       TRUE  FALSE TRUE  FALSE 
#>  5 tamper                    sensors       TRUE  FALSE TRUE  FALSE 
#>  6 motion_area_configuration motion_areas  TRUE  TRUE  TRUE  TRUE  
#>  7 motion_area_candidate     motion_areas  TRUE  FALSE FALSE FALSE 
#>  8 convenience_area_motion   motion_areas  TRUE  FALSE TRUE  FALSE 
#>  9 security_area_motion      motion_areas  TRUE  FALSE TRUE  FALSE 
#> 10 wifi_connectivity         connectivity  TRUE  FALSE TRUE  FALSE 
#> 11 speaker                   entertainment TRUE  FALSE TRUE  FALSE

Controlling Lights and Building Payloads

hue_payload_light() constructs validated CLIP API v2 update payloads for hue_update_light() and hue_update_grouped_light():

payload <- hue_payload_light(
  on = TRUE,
  brightness = 75,
  mirek = 320,
  dynamics_duration = 500
)
str(payload)
#> List of 4
#>  $ on               :List of 1
#>   ..$ on: logi TRUE
#>  $ dimming          :List of 1
#>   ..$ brightness: num 75
#>  $ color_temperature:List of 1
#>   ..$ mirek: int 320
#>  $ dynamics         :List of 1
#>   ..$ duration: int 500
lights <- hue_get_lights()
hue_update_light(lights$id[[1]], body = payload)

# Recall a scene with a 1-second transition
scenes <- hue_get_scenes()
hue_recall_scene(scenes$id[[1]], action = "active", duration = 1000)

Working with Nested JSON Responses

Every API response from huer is parsed through hue_parse_response() into a tibble. Scalar and nested object properties are flattened into dot-separated columns automatically, while nested arrays (such as children, services, or actions) are stored as list-columns that can be expanded cleanly with hue_unnest_array():

sample_room <- paste0(
  '{"errors":[],"data":[{"id":"room-01","type":"room",',
  '"metadata":{"name":"Living Room","archetype":"living_room"},',
  '"children":[',
  '{"rid":"dev-01","rtype":"device"},',
  '{"rid":"dev-02","rtype":"device"}],',
  '"services":[{"rid":"gl-01","rtype":"grouped_light"}]}]}'
)

rooms <- hue_parse_response(sample_room)
rooms
#> # A tibble: 1 × 6
#>   id      type  metadata.name metadata.archetype children         services
#>   <chr>   <chr> <chr>         <chr>              <list>           <list>  
#> 1 room-01 room  Living Room   living_room        <tibble [2 × 2]> <tibble>

# Expand nested array list-columns
hue_unnest_array(rooms, "children")
#> # A tibble: 2 × 7
#>   id      type  metadata.name metadata.archetype services         rid    rtype 
#>   <chr>   <chr> <chr>         <chr>              <list>           <chr>  <chr> 
#> 1 room-01 room  Living Room   living_room        <tibble [1 × 2]> dev-01 device
#> 2 room-01 room  Living Room   living_room        <tibble [1 × 2]> dev-02 device
hue_unnest_array(rooms, "services")
#> # A tibble: 1 × 7
#>   id      type  metadata.name metadata.archetype children         rid   rtype   
#>   <chr>   <chr> <chr>         <chr>              <list>           <chr> <chr>   
#> 1 room-01 room  Living Room   living_room        <tibble [2 × 2]> gl-01 grouped…

Set tidy = FALSE on any endpoint call if you prefer the raw parsed R list.

Hue Bridge Pro MotionAware & Real-Time EventStream

Bridge Pro turns compatible lights into MotionAware virtual motion areas. You can manage configurations and read convenience/security motion states directly, or subscribe to real-time updates over Server-Sent Events (GET /eventstream/clip/v2):

# Bridge Pro MotionAware resources
candidates <- hue_get_motion_area_candidates()
configs <- hue_get_motion_area_configurations()
convenience <- hue_get_convenience_area_motions()
security <- hue_get_security_area_motions()

# Stream live events over SSE
events <- hue_eventstream(max_events = 5L, timeout = 30)
